t: In the case of the authorization contained in the table in section 2201(a) of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012 (division B of Public Law 112–81; 125 Stat. 1666) for Kitsap, Washington, for construction of Explosives Handling Wharf No. 2, the Secretary of the Navy may construct new hardened facilities in lieu of hardening existing structures and a new facility to replace the existing Coast Guard Maritime Force Protection Unit and the Naval Undersea Warfare Command unhardened facilities using appropriations available for the project.

fable.w: This section only modifies the scope of a previously authorized military construction project, letting the Secretary of the Navy build new facilities using available appropriations. The mention of the Coast Guard and Naval Undersea Warfare Command might suggest coordination, but both are federal entities and no consultation is required anyway. No outside party, public comment, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is involved.
fable.s: the Secretary of the Navy may construct new hardened facilities in lieu of hardening existing structures

qwen_block.w: This section grants the Secretary of the Navy discretion to choose between construction methods (new facilities vs. hardening existing ones) for a military project. It does not require consultation with, or participation by, any non-federal entities such as the public, states, or private organizations. The mention of the Coast Guard and Naval Undersea Warfare Command refers to internal federal agencies, so any coordination is intra-governmental.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of the Navy may construct new hardened facilities in lieu of hardening existing structures and a new facility to replace the existing Coast Guard Maritime Force Protection Unit and the Naval Undersea Warfare Command unhardened facilities using appropriations available for the project.

opus.w: This section changes the scope of a military construction authorization so the Navy can build new hardened facilities instead of hardening existing ones. The only actors named are federal entities (the Navy, the Coast Guard, and the Naval Undersea Warfare Command). No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, and the section creates no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, or right to sue.
opus.s: the Secretary of the Navy may construct new hardened facilities in lieu of hardening existing structures

qwen_chat.w: This section grants the Secretary of the Navy discretion to alter the scope of a construction project using existing appropriations. It does not require or recommend consultation with any outside parties, such as state governments, the public, or private entities. The decision is made internally by a federal official.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of the Navy may construct new hardened facilities in lieu of hardening existing structures and a new facility to replace the existing Coast Guard Maritime Force Protection Unit and the Naval Undersea Warfare Command unhardened facilities using appropriations available for the project.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "in lieu of" implies a choice or consultation, but the text simply grants the Secretary discretion to use funds differently. There is no mention of consulting with outside parties, holding hearings, or involving non-federal entities in the decision-making process. The actors involved are the Secretary of the Navy and the federal appropriations.
